newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to formally seek WTO panel in Japan film case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to formally seek WTO panel in Japan film case.

text.p: The United States plans to formally ask the World Trade Organization on Friday to create a dispute settlement panel to rule on a complaint about access to Japan's film and photographic paper markets, U.S. trade officials said Thursday.
U.S. trade officials said a panel is likely to be formed in late October and it will take several months before a decision can be made, so a ruling on the dispute may not be issued until mid-May.
Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd is Kodak's primary competitor in Japan.

U.S. officials have said they would seek a total of three panels in a case involving Eastman Kodak Co's complaint that Japanese government barriers kept foreign competitors out of much of Japan's film and photo paper markets.

In a statement issued through a spokesman, Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said that as a result of the U.S. investigation into Kodak's complaint "we have learned more about market barriers in the film sector than any other sector in the Japanese economy.
"The systematic barriers we have found in this sector are the types of trade barriers that pose a serious challenge to the international trading system," Barshefsky said in the statement.
The film case was one of a number of trade issues Barshefsky discussed with Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, during a meeting Thursday afternoon.

The United States is pursuing the Kodak case on three fronts. It is challenging what it says were government efforts to thwart Kodak, barriers to foreign suppliers created by Japan's Large Scale Retail Store Law and restrictive business practices.

Washington is pursuing further consultations with Japan on its retail store complaint and has accused Tokyo of resisting a request for consultations on the restrictive business practices issue, trade officials said.
